description.text: Emerentiana was a Roman virgin and martyr who lived around the beginning of the 4th century. According to tradition, she was the foster sister of Agnes of Rome, a wealthy heiress who was martyred for refusing an engagement because of her Christian faith. Emerentiana’s mother served as Agnes’s wet nurse and nanny, and after Agnes’s death, Emerentiana, still a catechumen, visited Agnes’s tomb to pray. While there, she was attacked by a pagan mob, professed her faith, and was stoned to death, thereby receiving a baptism of desire or blood.

Her cult has been known since antiquity, with references in the martyrologies of Jerome and Bede, and her crypt was discovered in the 19th century by Mariano Armellini. The feast day of 23 January was originally celebrated on 16 September in Jerome’s martyrology, but has since been confined to local calendars. She is commemorated in art, such as a marble relief by Ercole Ferrata in Sant’Agnese in Agone, and is invoked against colic and stomach ache.

curiosities.text: She is invoked against colic and stomach ache.
Her tomb is located in the church of Sant'Agnese fuori le mura in Rome.
She is represented in art as a young girl holding lilies and stones in her lap, or being stoned by a mob.
Her cult has been confined to local calendars since 1969.
She made a cameo appearance in Cardinal Nicholas Wiseman's novel Fabiola, mourning Agnes after her martyrdom.
